messages:
sara_support: customer report: Python streaming generator hung after a brief network blip during a long SSE response. They say the generator just stops yielding (no StopAsyncIteration) and billing shows connection still counted. Repro steps + logs below. /cc @matt_devex @lee_eng :rotating_light:

matt_devex: can you paste logs + exact SDK version + OS? Any traceback?

sara_support: condensed logs (snip):
```
[2026-03-15 14:02:10] GET /v1/stream -> 200
chunk: "data: {\"delta\":\"Hel""
chunk: "data: {\"delta\":\"lo\n"   <-- split in middle of token
chunk: "data: [keepalive]\n\n"
chunk: "data: {\"delta\":\" world\"}\n\n"
```
They run python 3.10 on ubuntu 22.04, SDK reported: redwood==0.8.3.

lee_eng: interesting — looks like partial JSON event crossing chunk boundary. Could be parser waiting for newline delimiter. Which transport? SSE over HTTP/1.1 chunked?

sara_support: yes, Content-Type: text/event-stream, HTTP/1.1, nginx LB in front. Repro steps: 
1) run example below
2) after ~2s kill conn (tcp kill -9) then bring back
3) generator does not resume, hangs forever

```
from redwood import Client
c = Client(api_key=MY_KEY)
for event in c.stream("gpt-small","hello"):
    print(event)
```

nicole_oncall: @lee_eng @matt_devex assigning oncall — what SDK patch lines up with our runtime change? Any known fixes in 0.9.x?

matt_devex: there's a parser fix in 0.9.0 that handles mid-event chunk assembly and explicit keepalive tokens. If they're on 0.8.3, they hit a known bug where partial buffer isn't flushed on reconnect. Ask customer to try 0.9.1.

sara_support: asked customer to `pip install redwood==0.9.1` and retest, they said still seeing stalls but different symptoms — generator resumed but then raised ValueError from json.decoder at ~30% of stream.

lee_eng: can you get a full raw capture of the stream (tcpdump) or at least our client debug logs (set REDWOOD_LOG=debug)? Need exact chunk boundaries and where parser choked.

sara_support: pasted debug capture (snip):
```
DEBUG:stream:buf='data: {"delta":"Par'
DEBUG:stream:buf='data: {"delta":"tial"}\n\n'
DEBUG:stream:parse_event -> json.loads fails on 'data: {"delta":"Part'
```

matt_devex: aha — the parser expects event lines to start with `data: ` and then concatenates until blank line, but a keepalive message `data: [keepalive]` can appear in between and we didn't handle merging across. Proposed quick patch:
```
# pseudo-patch
while True:
    chunk = sock.recv(1024)
    buf += chunk.decode('utf-8')
    # split into events on double newline
    parts = buf.split('\n\n')
    for p in parts[:-1]:
        lines = [l for l in p.split('\n') if not l.startswith('data: [keepalive]')]
        if lines:
            event_json = ''.join(l.replace('data: ', '') for l in lines)
            yield json.loads(event_json)
    buf = parts[-1]
```

lee_eng: long term, runtime team should add explicit event reassembly in the low-level reader. @deploy-bot can we create eng-runtime ticket?

deploy-bot: Created ENG-RUNTIME-4567: "SSE parser: handle keepalive and partial event reassembly" — assigned to lee_eng. Link: https://ourtracker/ENG-RUNTIME-4567

nicole_oncall: customer is on Dedicated and seeing billing increments during hang — billing team copied. For now advise them to set `stream(retry=False)` or have LB drop long-idle sockets as workaround.

sara_support: customer confirmed `pip install redwood==0.9.1` + apply workaround `for e in client.stream(..., retry=False):` allowed them to get through with manual reconnect logic. They accepted workaround but asked for ETA.

lee_eng: estimate for patch -> small PR + tests, target release 0.9.2 in 1 week. Will include unit test that simulates keepalive in middle of event and simulated reconnect.

matt_devex: adding note to changelog and support KB: "Streaming generator hung after network blip — upgrade to 0.9.1 or 0.9.2 when released, workaround: retry=False + reconnect loop." :white_check_mark:

sara_support: thanks team — closing once 0.9.2 merges and customer is notified. :pray:
